ts diagnostics¶

diagnostics describes a series before a model is chosen: its autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions, and the tests that read them — the Ljung–Box test for white noise, the augmented Dickey–Fuller and KPSS tests for a unit root and for stationarity, and the ARCH-LM test for volatility clustering.

The tests return a result struct holding the statistic, its p-value, the critical value at the requested level and a reject flag; ljung_box returns one entry per requested lag set. The two unit-root tests have opposite null hypotheses (ADF: a unit root; KPSS: stationarity), so use them together.

The Surface¶

Entity

What it gives you

acf

The sample autocorrelation function of a series: its correlation with itself at lags 0 through max_lag

AcfOptions

Options of ts::acf

adf_test

The augmented Dickey–Fuller test for a unit root

AdfOptions

Options of ts::adf_test

AdfResult

Result of ts::adf_test

arch_lm

Engle’s ARCH-LM test for volatility clustering: are the squared values of a series autocorrelated?

ArchLmOptions

Options of ts::arch_lm

ArchLmResult

Result of ts::arch_lm

kpss_test

The KPSS test of the null that a series is stationary around a level or a trend

KpssOptions

Options of ts::kpss_test

KpssResult

Result of ts::kpss_test

ljung_box

The Ljung–Box test that a series, or a model’s residuals, is white noise up to a set of lags

LjungBoxOptions

Options of ts::ljung_box

LjungBoxResult

Result of ts::ljung_box

pacf

The sample partial autocorrelation function: the correlation at each lag that remains after removing the effect of the shorter lags

PacfOptions

Options of ts::pacf

How To Call It¶

Compute the autocorrelations of an autoregressive series and test whether it is white noise.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const auto e = noise(200);
  std::vector<double> x(200);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < 200; ++t) {
    carry = 0.7 * carry + e[t];
    x[t] = carry;
  }
  const Series y = pluss::make_series(x, {200}, f64);

  ts::AcfOptions options;
  options.max_lag = 4;
  show("acf", ts::acf(y, options));
  const auto test = ts::ljung_box(y);
  std::cout << "Ljung-Box p-value = " << test.pvalue.host<double>()[0] << "\n";
}

Output

acf              1.0000   0.6502   0.4426   0.4037   0.3413
Ljung-Box p-value = 0.0000
